- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slightly rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast growth to 2–3% per period to avoid overcorrection.  
- If official event net supply is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model often underestimates upside — increase forecast baseline by 1–2% to reflect bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, reverse direction — model often misreads sentiment, so reduce forecast slope or shift to downward trend.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10d average, reduce by 1–2% per period to align with historical volatility.  
- When multiple auction events occur in short window (e.g., 3+ events in 7d), model tends to overreact — dampen forecast growth by 1–2% per event to avoid overfitting to supply shocks.
